# PiTTy v0.5.25

## UI Responsiveness Under High-Volume Tool Output

- Intermediate `tool_execution_update` events are now coalesced per tool call with a 50 ms flush window, so long-running commands that stream hundreds of cumulative-output updates no longer saturate the UI thread, delay the heartbeat, or block typing and scrolling.
- Final tool results (`tool_execution_end`) still apply immediately; pending updates are flushed before lifecycle events, extension dialogs, and cleanup so event ordering and output content are preserved.
- Updates without a tool call id bypass coalescing and apply immediately; the pending map is bounded to 512 distinct tool calls and flushes before the bound is exceeded.
- The footer now reports truthful `ready`/`working` status at the readiness boundary instead of lingering on a stale status until the next refresh.

## Live Subagent Polling Efficiency

- Subagent refresh, activity precedence, and JSONL tail parsing are consolidated into shared helpers, removing duplicated polling logic.
- Parsed transcript records are cached by file mtime and size in a bounded LRU cache, so the 750 ms subagent poller no longer re-reads megabytes of unchanged transcripts every tick; the inspector invalidates cached reads when the transcript file or step activity changes.
- Live transcript discovery for running children without status/session paths is preserved.

## Validation

- Full suite passes with 324 tests passed and 1 platform-specific test skipped; typecheck clean.
